text:
sarah: Heads-up — EU GPU pool is 75% saturated and we're seeing bursts of 5xx/timeout on Dedicated inference routes. Error pattern points to encryptor-proxy failing KMS decrypts in privnet-eu, causing tokenization cold-paths and large latency spikes. Logs look noisy: `decrypt error: KMS403 InvalidToken`

raj: saw the same in dashboards, thanks for flagging. Is this the encryptor-proxy rollout from last night? @marta @emma can you confirm?

ops-bot: deploy/infra #4829 rolled out `encryptor-proxy:v2.4.1` to privnet-eu at 2026-03-19T22:14:03Z (canary: 100%).

marta: yep that was my change — tightened egress rules for privnet to stop broad outbound ranges. I added deny to 172.16.0.0/12 and tightened NAT gateway access; didn't expect DNS->internal KMS endpoints to be affected.

luke: we observed KMS 403s from the proxy, then fallback to 'local cache miss' path which causes an expensive GPU rehydrate sequence. Cache was tiny on those nodes (default 64KB), so many decrypts hit KMS.

emma: mitigation proposal: rollback the proxy config to the previous policy, open outbound 443 to `kms.eu.internal.redwood` and `hsm-priv.eu.redwood` for the short-term, and enable auditlog sampling at 50% so we don't overwhelm the collector while restoring. Rolling a canary now.

sarah: +1 to revert ASAP. Note the cost tradeoff: leaving egress wide increases KMS egress (est ~120k/mo) and will raise NAT costs. But SLA impact for Dedicated customers if we don't revert is worse (we're already seeing token latency >500ms).

marta: started partial rollback on privnet-eu — patch applied to 4/12 encryptor-proxy instances (canary). Running a quick healthcheck: 
```bash
# quick probe
curl -sS -H "Host: encryptor-proxy" https://privnet-eu/healthz || true
```
Output: 4/4 proxies OK, upstream KMS tls handshake successful, decrypt latency median ~120ms.

infra-bot: healthcheck results for privnet-eu canary: 4/4 ok, avg latency 118ms, error-rate reduced from 6% -> 0.5%. Alert suppression queued for 15m.

raj: OK, rollback looks healthy. Next steps (short): 1) add an explicit IaC allow rule for `kms.eu.internal.redwood:443` with `iam:SourceIdentity` condition, 2) increase encryptor-proxy local cache TTL and size (suggest 6h, 8MB), 3) add a firewall exception test to CI that hits KMS endpoints. I'll open PRs.

emma: also add an audit-log tag on these decrypt calls so we can correlate customer impact -> policy change quickly. Lower sampling for now to avoid log collector bursts.

sarah: good. please call out cost delta in the PR. We need exec sign-off for >100k/mo variance. I'll draft a customer blurb noting transient latency and the rollback.

marta: noted. re: long-term, we should investigate replicating KMS metadata into a regional read-only cache to avoid egress for short-lived decrypts. Might be an infra + security discussion (HSM/KMS replication).

raj: filed: https://redwood.internal/infra/PR-5421 "privnet-eu: explicit kms egress allow + encryptor-proxy cache sizing" — assigns: @raj, reviewers @emma @marta. Includes cost appendix and rollforward plan.

sarah: thanks team. If anything flares during the rollback window ping me on call. :thumbsup:

luke: quick note for runbook update — add a step to check proxy cache size and KMS throttle counters before scaling GPU pools; will send a tiny PR.

ops-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-1123 "privnet-eu encryptor-proxy egress policy caused KMS decrypt failures -> GPU tokenization latency" (status: mitigation in progress).

sarah: closing loop here for now. We'll reconvene if error-rate doesn't stay <1% after full rollback.
